data.title: Monetization: the core stays MIT and free forever; organisations pay $10 per active person a month for one view across their repositories
data.why: Every neighbour that charges (Mainline, Hamster, Kaiku) does it with a layer on top, never the local tool; the core's promise (no server, no account, no network, a format nobody gates) stays intact only if the paid part is the aggregate across repositories. A seat is a distinct git email with an event in the last 30 days in the org view; agents are never seats (Linear and GitHub's precedent; 90% of this journal's events are agent-written). Up to 3 repositories and 10 people are free, so the 3-8 team the strategy targets never pays. $10 is the floor of the tracker band (Linear Basic $10, Copilot Business $19). Nothing is built before evidence: E1 money questions in Probe B, E2 prepaid hand-run cross-repo pilots, E3 a /pricing fake door; then G1 > 0.
data.rejected: Licence by company size, Docker-style: breaks MIT forever, and Beads and Backlog.md are free, so users would switch; A paid local multi-repo command with an offline licence key: anyone can rebuild it from the MIT core, and it is the features-removed edition roadmap section 5 forbids; Billing agents as seats: punishes the agent use the product exists for and multiplies the bill; SSO or audit as the paid trigger: its buyer is outside the ICP (not for teams over 20 asking for SSO); Flat price per organisation (Sentry Team, Sidekiq Pro): not chosen yet, kept as a comparison arm in E1 interviews
